paras: The lynching of John C. Wells was the reported killing of a Canadian man at Bad Axe, Michigan, by friends of a neighbor whom Wells was said to have killed in a quarrel over a ditch. It was known to the press only through a wire telegram from Kingston, Ontario, in January 1888, which said the matter would be brought to the attention of the Dominion Government.

According to the Kingston dispatch of January 24, 1888, Wells killed a neighbor in a quarrel about a ditch, and the neighbor's friends then lynched him. The dispatch did not give the date of either killing, the neighbor's name, the number of men involved or how Wells was killed, and it did not state Wells's race.

The same telegram reported that the attention of the Dominion Government would be called to the lynching of Wells as a Canadian. No report of an inquest, arrests or a Canadian inquiry appears in the coverage.

The story circulated as a two-sentence brief among unrelated telegrams, and its news value lay in the Canadian angle rather than in the killing itself. The Richmond Daily Times ran it on January 25 in a column of "Short Telegrams," spelling the town "Bad Ax." The Maysville Evening Bulletin printed the same text the same day under the headline "Canada Will Investigate," with a January 25 dateline. A week later the Connecticut Western News included it, as "Badaxe," in a news-in-brief column.
None of the papers commented on the lynching, and the coverage includes no account from a Michigan paper.

reader.title: Lynching of John C. Wells
bases: The only report describes John C. Wells as lynched by the friends of a neighbor he had killed (A1).

The brief says the neighbor's friends 'lynched' Wells after he killed the neighbor, which states an extralegal killing in retaliation for an alleged crime (A1); the number of 'friends' is not given and no detail of the act appears, so the group size and circumstances cannot be confirmed.
All three items carry the same Kingston, Ont., wire text (A1, A2, A3), so they are one report, and no Michigan or other independent account was found.
